column1: # Fuchin Temple, Nyunpa's trial and passing, Xian village and martial arts school. Original chronology and branch-specific endings preserved.

column3: The forest has cut us\noff from the road.{page_break}I fear I may never\nsee home again.{end_wait}
Did you know Mogall\nwas once open grassland?{end_now}
They say the trees\ngrew in a single night.{page_break}Nyunpa alone knows\nhow to cross safely.{end_wait}
I saw stones falling\nfrom the night sky.{page_break}The forest changed\nsoon after that.{end_wait}

Om...{pause_20_skippable} Om...
The northern sky
burned blue.{page_break}Stones fell like rain.
The woods swallowed
the old road.{end_wait}

The falling stones
and strange blue light
trouble the monks.{page_break}Our oldest scrolls
speak of such signs.{end_wait}

Nyunpa has refused
food for days.{page_break}His hands tremble.
He says he must
continue fasting.{end_wait}
Is it noble to give\nyour life seeking\nenlightenment?{end_now}
I respect his faith.\nI still wish he'd eat.\nWe need him alive.{end_wait}
I won't cross the\nforest alone.{page_break}Even the monks fear\nwhat lives there.{end_wait}
The scrolls speak of\nstars falling to earth.{page_break}I never believed\nI'd see it myself.{end_wait}
If disaster is coming,\nwhy do we still train?{page_break}I don't know whether\nto fight or run.{end_wait}
I tried fasting once.\nBy evening I could\nthink of nothing else.{end_wait}

I want to become
a worthy monk.{page_break}But I hope wisdom
doesn't demand
my death.{end_wait}
Who is there?\nWho speaks inside\nmy thoughts?{end_wait}
Then I cannot help.\nYou should turn back\nwhile you still can.{end_wait}
The grotto is open\nto you now.{page_break}Be careful below\nthe waterfall.{end_wait}
Speak to the monk\nbeneath the falls.\nHe guards the trial.{end_wait}
Do you take pleasure\nin reading the minds\nof strangers?{end_now}
Listen too often,\nand you may learn\nthings you regret.{end_wait}
Then you understand\nthat a thought is\nnot always a wish.{end_wait}
Nyunpa has told me\nabout your trial.\nYou may enter.{end_wait}
Fuchin Falls tests\nmore than strength.{page_break}Enter only when\nyou are ready.{end_wait}
Those travelers look\nyoung to face the\nwaterfall grotto.{end_wait}
Have you finished\nthe grotto trial?{end_now}
You learned the\nsecret of Ki?{end_wait}
Nyunpa is waiting\nfor you inside.{end_wait}
Master Nyunpa waits\nat the temple.{page_break}Go to him now.{end_wait}
The travelers have\npassed the trial.{page_break}Nyunpa will surely\nbe pleased.{end_wait}
You have done well\nto master our art.{end_wait}
We call this power\nKi at Fuchin Temple.{end_wait}
You have shown\npatience and wisdom.{page_break}But there is more\nyou should know.{end_wait}
As promised, I will\nshow you the way.{page_break}Use this power\nwithin the forest.{end_wait}
What might happen\nif you used Force\namong the trees?{end_wait}
Ha! Still curious,\nI see.{end_now}
Strength is useful.\nBut not every path\nopens through battle.{end_wait}
Good. There is no\nwisdom in needless\nviolence.{end_wait}
The beasts will flee\nwhen they know\nyou can see them.{end_wait}
The creatures know\ntheir own forest.{page_break}Follow their path\nand you may survive.{end_wait}
Use Force to reveal\nthe hidden beasts.{page_break}Follow them through\nthe trees.{end_wait}
Nyunpa seems at peace.{page_break}Do not waste\nwhat he taught you.{end_wait}
We cannot leave\neverything to strangers.{page_break}We must learn\nto help ourselves.{end_wait}
It used to be quiet\nhere at the temple.{page_break}Now every traveler\nbrings fearful news.{end_wait}
Master Nyunpa...\nHe's gone.{end_wait}
He grew so thin\nin his final days.{page_break}I wish he'd let\nus care for him.{end_wait}
I used to believe\nhe'd watch over us.{page_break}Now I don't know\nwhat to believe.{end_wait}

Stones from the sky.
Mountains in flames.
The sea in turmoil.{page_break}Even this temple
may not be safe.{end_wait}

I knew his fasting
might kill him.{page_break}Knowing that didn't
make it easier
to watch.{end_wait}
Nyunpa found peace\nbefore he died.{page_break}I hope that peace\nwas worth the cost.{end_wait}
He was scarcely\nmore than skin\nand bone.{end_wait}
He still had so\nmuch to teach us.{page_break}Who will guide\nthe younger monks?{end_wait}
The dragon's flame\nlights the way\nthrough darkness.{end_wait}
Those who seek truth\nmay discover\nthe secret of Ki.{end_wait}
Light reveals\nwhat darkness hides.{end_wait}
A stone dragon\nwithout eyes.{page_break}Something once fit\ninside the sockets.{end_wait}
The dragon's eyes\nglow a deep red.{end_wait}
Welcome to Xian.\nTravelers are rare\nthese days.{end_wait}
You crossed Mogall\nForest alive?{end_now}
That's no small feat.\nYou must be skilled.{end_wait}
Xian is known\nfor its fine silk.{page_break}Our families have\nworked it for years.{end_wait}

Thieves trouble
the roads now.{page_break}They avoid Xian.
Master Feh sees
to that.{end_wait}
Master Feh teaches\nmartial arts here.{page_break}His students keep\nour village safe.{end_wait}
Martial arts are\na part of life\nin Xian.{end_wait}
You should visit\nMaster Feh's school.{page_break}He may teach you\nsomething useful.{end_wait}
My clothes aren't silk.\nOnly the wealthy\ncan afford it.{end_wait}
My kung fu improves\na little each day.{page_break}Master Feh says\npatience matters.{end_wait}
The roads are unsafe.\nStill, I trust\nour fighters.{end_wait}
These mulberry trees\nfeed the silkworms.{page_break}Without them,\nXian would suffer.{end_wait}
Are you warriors\nfrom Master Feh's\nschool?{end_now}
Then I wish you\nstrength on the\nwestern road.{end_wait}
At least you know\nyour limits.{page_break}That's more than\nmost fighters admit.{end_wait}
Watch where you're\nstanding! You made\nme spill the water!{end_wait}
Now I must fill\nthese buckets again.{page_break}My back can't take\nmuch more of this.{end_wait}
Please, stand clear.\nI can't afford\nto spill this.{end_wait}
The tree moved!\nDid you see that?{end_wait}
It moved again...\nPerhaps I need\nsome rest.{end_wait}
Those children came\nto study at\nMaster Feh's school.{end_wait}
I hope our silk\nreaches new markets\nwhen the road opens.{end_wait}
A strong fist means\nnothing without\ngood judgment.{end_wait}
Master Feh trains\nus hard.{page_break}He says discipline\ncomes before strength.{end_wait}
Silk is soft,\nbut the work that\nmakes it is hard.{end_wait}
Master Feh shouted,\nand the thieves ran.{page_break}No one here\nhas forgotten it.{end_wait}
These trees keep\nour village alive.{page_break}We guard them\nas carefully as homes.{end_wait}
Traveling west alone\nis dangerous.{page_break}I'll wait until\nI find companions.{end_wait}
I carry water\nevery morning.{page_break}The work never ends.{end_wait}
You know how to fight.\nBut could you work\nthese fields all day?{end_wait}
The harvest leaves\nmy shoulders aching.{page_break}Still, we need\nthe silk.{end_wait}
Our silk travels\nwest to Tolbi.{page_break}When the road closes,\nour wages vanish.{end_wait}
Silk Road leads\ntoward Tolbi.{page_break}It takes many days\nto reach the city.{end_wait}
We depend on\nthe silk merchants.{page_break}Without them,\nour stalls sit empty.{end_wait}
I've heard Tolbi\nis a beautiful city.{page_break}I wonder if\nI'll ever see it.{end_wait}
Altin's mine supplies\nmetal and precious\nstones.{end_wait}
Altin's miners are\ntough people.{page_break}Their work demands\nit of them.{end_wait}
Mining is dangerous.\nSkill matters more\nthan brute strength.{end_wait}
Warriors use weapons.\nOur students learn\nto evade and strike.{end_wait}
Our armor is made\nfor quick movement.{page_break}It may not suit\nyour fighting style.{end_wait}
We make much of\nwhat we need here.{page_break}Xian's craftsmen\ntake pride in that.{end_wait}

A traveler should
learn the customs
of each town.{page_break}Fighting isn't
all there is.{end_wait}
Merchants once came\nhere every week.{page_break}Now the road is quiet.\nSomething is wrong.{end_wait}
Most of our guests\nare from Xian.{page_break}Where have all\nthe travelers gone?{end_wait}
Respect the customs\nof the places\nyou visit.{end_wait}
When merchants arrive,\nour tables fill.{page_break}Without them,\nwe barely survive.{end_wait}
Fewer travelers\nmeans fewer meals\nserved here.{end_wait}
Welcome to\nMaster Feh's school.{page_break}Are you here\nto observe?{end_now}
Then please be quiet.\nThe lesson has begun.{end_wait}
Even armed warriors\ncan learn from\nmartial artists.{end_wait}
Kick from the hip.\nKeep your balance.\nThen strike again.{end_wait}

I train every day.
My fists still ache.{page_break}Master Feh says
that means I must
train carefully.{end_wait}
Speed and balance\nmatter as much\nas strength.{end_wait}
Many people in Xian\npractice martial arts.{page_break}Master Feh trains\nthe most dedicated.{end_wait}
Watching is useful.\nPractice is what\nmakes it yours.{end_wait}
Master Feh is busy.\nDo you still wish\nto speak with him?{end_now}
